items.caption: A modern drawing of 面 in seal-script style. This form represents the face character; the oracle graph is analyzed as an enclosing outline with an eye.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 面, drawn with a broad outer enclosure around an inner shape.
items.selection_reason: Shows the entry character in seal-script style and supports the distinction between its face graph and the separate flour and noodle word.

items.caption: A modern drawing of 麵 in seal-script style. The dictionary records 麪 as the Shuowen form, analyzed with 麥 for meaning and 丏 for sound, and 麵 as a later common spelling.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 麵, with 麥 on the left and a tall enclosed form on the right.
items.selection_reason: Helps distinguish the separate flour and noodle graph from 面’s face history; in simplified Chinese, 面 is used as its counterpart.

limitations.text: These are modern vector drawings in seal-script style, not images of dated artifacts. Their shapes do not establish the chronology or path between the recorded forms.
